name: sg-chrome
summary: Full-bleed hero running shader.gallery's chrome: the whole frame is one sheet of liquid metal rolling in slow swells. A domain-warped height field is shaded as a true mirror of a studio -- a hard horizon, a near-black floor and a stack of sharp strip lights -- so every crest carries a hot specular ridge and every valley sinks to shadow. Not a shard on black like liquid-metal: the metal is the ground, and the copy sits on a smoked panel over it.

colors.description: Four poles. c1 is the sky above the horizon, one rim light and the faint body tint; c2 the middle strip light and the warm rim; c3 the two big strip lights; c4 the floor and the deep sky overhead. Keep c4 dark, or the horizon the mirror depends on goes and the sheet reads as grey satin. Falls back to --fx-c1..--fx-c4.

flow.description: How fast the metal rolls and folds; 0 freezes the surface. Upstream default, range 0 to 1.2.

relief.description: Height of the swells. Low is a near-flat sheet showing the horizon, high tilts the reflections hard into the strip lights. Upstream default, range 0.2 to 2.5.

ripple.description: Domain-warp folding of the surface. Low is broad rolling swells, high is tight ferrofluid ridges. Upstream default, range 0 to 2.

gloss.description: Sharpness of the reflected light bands and speculars. Low is a satin brushed finish, high is a hard mirror. Upstream default, range 0 to 1.

mouseInfluence.description: How strongly the pointer pushes a bulge into the metal; 0 ignores the mouse. Upstream default, range 0 to 1. The shared runtime holds u_mouse at (0,0), so raising this on its own changes nothing.

deviations.what: The four u_palette colours are ours, not upstream's `nocturne` preset.
deviations.why: chrome/meta.json declares `defaultPalette: "nocturne"`, and the preset table lives in @shader-gallery/runtime, a package paw-fx does not vendor and which is not in the pinned repo. The port cannot resolve the name, so it ships four of its own and declares them. The shader's zero-fallback branch is not the answer either: paletteFor never produces zeros, so that branch is unreachable from paw-fx. Same call sg-gloam, sg-bask, sg-nebula-drift, sg-obsidian and sg-lightleak made.

deviations.what: No post chain: upstream's poster runs grain 0.04, aberration 0.002, vignette 0.3, contrast 1.08 and saturation 1.05 over the shader output.
deviations.why: The post chain lives in @shader-gallery/runtime, a package paw-fx does not vendor. Our output is the raw shader, so it will not match the upstream poster; the missing 0.3 vignette is the most visible gap, since it darkens the corners the strip lights otherwise run into. The section's own CSS grain layer covers what the poster's grain was there for.

deviations.what: Rendered through paw-fx's own WebGL runtime (effects/_shared/glsl-mount.js) rather than @shader-gallery/runtime.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream ships the .frag with no module around it. The GLSL itself is byte-identical to upstream and lives in shader.frag beside index.js.
